canonical_question: How does the wear rate of the RHEA film compare to other refractory HEAs reported in literature, given the claim of 'superior properties'?

question_variants.question: How does the wear rate of the RHEA film compare to other refractory HEAs reported in literature, given the claim of 'superior properties'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper compares the RHEA film directly to 304 stainless steel, stating the COF is 2 times lower and wear rate is 2-10 times lower at both RT and 300 °C. It does not provide data comparing the film to other refractory HEAs reported in literature.

answers.answer: The RHEA film showed a COF 2 times lower at RT and wear rate 2 times lower at RT and 300 °C than those of 304 stainless steel. No data is provided for comparison with other refractory HEAs.
answers.measurement_outcome: COF 2x lower; wear rate 2-10x lower compared to 304 SS
answers.mechanism: Superior wear properties compared to stainless steel
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison data for other refractory HEAs in literature.
evidence_spans: In this work, a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film of equimolar CuMoTaWV was deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates using DC-magnetron sputtering.
A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.
